text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- French President Jacques Chirac reaffirms Europe's support for setting up a Palestinian state and asks Israel to fulfill its obligations. Chirac in a speech to the Palestinian legistative council: no peace without solving the issue of Jerusalem because the city belongs to all religions and all humanity. We request the Palestinians hold on to peace and set up a democratic state.

- Cabinet decrees cancelling tariffs and fiscal stamps on electricity bills amounting to 100 kilowatt hours. Ministry of Religious Endownments to absorb 30,000 local mosques within the next five years and will hire 6,500 graduates of Al-Azhar Islamic university to preach at them.

- A wide-ranging ministerial meeting reviews the decisions of the executive council for the Middle East economic summit. Prime Minister Ganzouri to head a meeting which will decide today on Egypt's proposals in the summit.
- Egypt's Attorney General examines more than 75 antiquities in storage at Christies' auction house looking for stolen objects which have disappeared in London.
AL-AKHBAR
- President Mubarak and Chirac to hold talks tomorrow (Friday) on the developments in the peace process.
- Cabinet cuts 20 percent off electricity bills for the income-impaired. New cabinet decrees to confront destructive ideas and protect Islam.

- Electricity and Energy Minister Maher Abaza announced setting up a national project to extend the electricity network along the Alexandria-Cairo desert highway; will also allocate electricity to reclaim land.
- Prosecutor's office orders the confiscation of the library of English archeologist Ferdinand Duboni on suspicion that it contains antiquities.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Chirac announces his support for the Palestinians infront of their legistative council.
- Seven committees begin work today on building the Sheikh Zayed Canal and study increasing the agricultural lands along it to one million acres.
- Toshka canal is filled and the Nile flood water is flowing down to the natural depressions in the desert.
- Police find several antiquities and rare documents relating to the Suez Canal in the house of a wood trader.
AL-WAFD
- Egypt has finally cracked down on Shi'ites, a front page editorial says.
